stories.headline: Odisha shuts schools, Anganwadi centres in six districts from November 19 to 21 amid Cyclone Akvan
stories.title: Odisha shuts schools, Anganwadi centres in six districts from November 19 to 21 amid Cyclone Akvan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Bhubaneswar: The Odisha government has ordered the closure of all government, government-aided and private schools, along with Anganwadi centres, in six districts from November 19 to 21 in view of Cyclone Akvan.

The decision comes as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasts that the severe cyclonic storm is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and South Odisha coasts by noon on November 20.
According to the IMD, the cyclone was over the central parts of the South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal at 8.30 am on Wednesday.
It moved north-northwestwards at a speed of 7 kmph during the preceding six hours.
The storm was located near latitude 12.9°N and longitude 85.4°E, about 710 km south of Gopalpur and 770 km south of Puri in Odisha.
The IMD has forecast that Cyclone Akvan will cross the coast between Narsapur and Puri as a severe cyclonic storm, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 90-100 kmph and gusts reaching 110 kmph.
The weather department has issued an Orange Message cyclone alert for the North Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and South Odisha coasts.
IMD Bhubaneswar director Manorama Mohanty provided an update on the cyclone's position, movement and expected landfall on Wednesday.
The Odisha government's school closure order is aimed at ensuring the safety of students and children at Anganwadi centres as the cyclone approaches the coast.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan shifts track again; T.N. may have to wait till November 23 for heavy rain
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan shifts track again; T.N. may have to wait till November 23 for heavy rain
stories.summary: In its latest forecast, the IMD has said cyclone Akvan has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and lies over westcentral and adjoining central parts of south Bay of Bengal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan has emerged as a complex weather system to track, with the India Meteorological Department revising its forecast track and likely landfall point again on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).
Tamil Nadu’s prospects of heavy rainfall have been pushed to November 23.
In its latest forecast, the IMD has said cyclone Akvan has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and lies over westcentral and adjoining central parts of south Bay of Bengal.
It is likely to move north-northwestwards and is likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by November 20 noon.
It will maintain strength as a severe cyclonic storm with maximum wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110kmph.
This is the third revision of the forecast on the cyclone’s trajectory since November 16.
Earlier, it was expected to make a landfall between Nellore and Tuni and then Nellore and Visakhapatnam.
The RMC has also revised the intensity of the system during landfall.
Cyclone Akvan is likely to hit the coast as a severe cyclonic storm, against the earlier forecast of a very severe cyclonic storm.
With the severe cyclonic storm climbing further north, chances for a widespread or intense rainfall over the State have diminished further.
The Regional Meteorological Centre has forecast isolated light rainfall to continue over ghat areas of Western Ghats districts till November 21.
One or two places in north coastal Tamil Nadu may get mild rainfall on November 21.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan's track and intensity remain uncertain as weather models diverge
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan's track and intensity remain uncertain as weather models diverge
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan in the Bay of Bengal is showing signs of unpredictable behaviour, with its movement slowing and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) downgrading its forecast peak intensity from a very severe cyclonic storm to a severe cyclonic storm.
Different weather models have also produced varying predictions for the storm's track and further intensification.
The projected landfall location has shifted further north in the IMD's latest updates.

At 11.30am on November 18, 2026 severe cyclonic storm Akvan was located about 540 kilometres south-east of Narsapur and 570 km east of Chennai, according to the latest IMD update posted on X (formerly Twitter).

The weather agency predicted that the cyclone could make landfall between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha around noon on November 20, with sustained wind speeds of 90–100 km per hour and gusts of up to 110 km/h.

In an earlier update, issued just a few hours before, the IMD had forecast landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, with sustained wind speeds of 100–110 km/h and gusts of up to 120 km/h.
During the night of November 17-18, the cyclone moved at speeds as low as 3km/h.
Its forward speed increased to 7-8 km/h on the morning of November 18, according to the IMD.
"However from November 18, the ridge to the east of the system is very likely to dominate leading to northwestwards to north-northwestward movement with higher translational speed," the agency added.
The IMD highlighted significant differences between weather models over the cyclone's movement, intensification, landfall location and timing.
"Regarding further intensification, there exist large uncertainty among different models," the IMD said.

Forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and artificial intelligence-based weather models suggested that the storm could weaken below tropical cyclone intensity before landfall, according to the IMD.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan threat eases as it is likely to weaken, heavy rain forecast
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan is expected to weaken before reaching the coast, reducing the risk of severe damage in Andhra Pradesh, while coastal districts remain under alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall on November 19 and 20.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The heavy to very heavy rainfall forecast for a few districts of Telangana was withdrawn as the cyclonic storm Akvan may not make its way to the State after it weakens into depression.

The cyclonic storm is likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), as per the latest information from India Meteorological Department (IMD).
While earlier observed and forecast track of the cyclone predicted it may enter Telangana, the latest track shows it may head to Odisha instead.

While the IMD-Hyderabad Centre on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall and thunderstorms accompanied by lightning as very likely to occur at isolated places in Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet and Mahabubabad on Friday, this was withdrawn.

According to its latest weather bulletin issued in the afternoon on Wednesday, only thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are predicted as very likely at isolated places in the four districts and in Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu and Nalgonda on Friday.
The same weather conditions may be witnessed in Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam and Suryapet on Thursday.

stories.headline: Don't keep us in the dark, don't humiliate us: Omar Abdullah to Centre on statehood
stories.title: Don't keep us in the dark, don't humiliate us: Omar Abdullah to Centre on statehood
stories.summary: Mendhar, Nov 18: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday attacked the BJP-led Centre over the denial of statehood to Jammu and Kashmir and wondered whether the party was deliberately deferring it till gets its own chief minister in the Union Territory. Abdullah said the repeated promise of statehood at an "appropriate time" has become meaningless. "If it is your wish not to restore statehood until the BJP has its own chief minister in Jammu and Kashmir, then say it openly. Tell the people clearly so that they are not kept under any illusion, and we are not humiliated repeatedly," he said, addressing a public rally in Mendhar township of Poonch district. The chief minister said it is more than two years since his government assumed office, but the Centre has yet to honour its commitment to restore statehood, which it had promised would be done after delimitation and the assembly election. "Even after waiting for two years and one month, we have been compelled to ask: Where has our state gone? Why is the restoration of statehood being delayed?" he asked. On the Centre's "appropriate time" deadline, Abdullah said, "What is the yardstick you have to measure this? What kind of scale will you use to decide that the time has finally come to restore our statehood?" He also accused the central dispensation of using security incidents to justify the continued delay, even though the elected government has no control over the police or law and order. Referring to the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and several terror incidents in Kulgam, Reasi, and Kishtwar over the past two years, the chief minister said the elected government is being made to account for failures in areas outside its jurisdiction. "We have no control over the police or law and order, yet we are told that because of the Pahalgam attack, perhaps statehood cannot be restored now. An incident takes place in Kulgam, and the same justification is given. An attack takes place in Reasi or Kishtwar, and again the same argument is put forward," he said. "How can you hold us responsible for matters over which we have no control? We have fulfilled our responsibilities in the areas entrusted to us. Why should the people of Jammu and Kashmir suffer for the failures of others? What kind of justice is this?" the National Conference leader added. Abdullah challenged the Centre to assess his government on infrastructure, healthcare, education and governance, rather than law and order, which is beyond its remit. "Either your intentions are not right, or you are not being sincere. If you do not want to restore statehood until the BJP gets its own chief minister, then have the courage to say so," he said. The chief minister also accused the Centre of deliberately reducing the standing of elected representatives by continuing the Union Territory arrangement. Pointing to protocol differences, Abdullah said the chief secretaries and chief justices enjoyed comparable status, but the chief ministers, ministers and MLAs of Union Territories are placed below their counterparts in states. "You do not want to weaken the chief secretary or undermine the chief justice. You want to weaken the people's elected government and humiliate their elected representatives," he said. Recalling the Centre's assurances before the Supreme Court during the proceedings concerning Article 370, he said the commitment was to restore statehood after delimitation, elections and the formation of an elected government. Abdullah said his government passed a resolution seeking restoration of statehood in its very first Cabinet meeting, and he personally submitted it to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said he has repeatedly reminded the prime minister of the commitment whenever he visited Jammu and Kashmir, including during the inauguration of the Sonamarg Tunnel and the Katra railway project, and also with Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Delhi. Despite the limitations, Abdullah said, his government neither used its restricted powers as an excuse nor backed away from its responsibilities. "We are not cowards who get frightened by difficult situations or use them as an excuse for our inability to deliver," he said.

stories.headline: Probe into Ahmedabad Air India crash in final stages, Centre tells SC
stories.title: Probe into Ahmedabad Air India crash in final stages, Centre tells SC
stories.summary: “We are at the fag end of the investigation,” Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
event term: 'chief justice of india' in summary weight 27.6
article_sentences: The Centre on Wednesday told the Supreme Court that the investigation into the June 2025 Air India crash in Ahmedabad that killed 260 people is in its final stages.
“We are at the fag end of the investigation,” Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.
“There is no reason why we should delay deliberately,” the top law officer said.
He urged the bench to adjourn the hearing by two to three weeks, saying the investigators had to follow international protocols.
The bench agreed to his request.
Appearing in the matter, advocate Prashant Bhushan pointed out that the final investigation report had not been made public yet and sought an early hearing.

On July 28 this year, the bench was told that the draft final report of the probe conducted by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) into the AI-171 crash in Ahmedabad on June 12, 2025, will be filed before it in the first week of October in a sealed cover.

The court was hearing petitions, including those filed by Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, the father of the deceased pilot, and the NGO ‘Safety Matters Foundation’, seeking an independent, court-monitored investigation into the crash.

The AAIB had said there is an “absolute statutory prohibition” on disclosing cockpit voice recordings and airborne image recordings from the Ahmedabad plane crash to any external committee or the public.
It said that sharing such material would violate Rules 17(1) and 17(5) read with Schedule C of the Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules, 2025.

Prior to this, the bench had asked the Centre to file a brief report on the “procedural protocol” followed so far, after it was informed that the investigation into the crash by the AAIB was at its fag end.
Air India's Boeing 787-8 flight AI171, en route to London's Gatwick Airport, was operated by pilot-in-command Captain Sumeet Sabharwal and co-pilot Captain Clive Kunder.

stories.headline: No India-US trade deal until new US tariff framework, Section 301 probe outcomes
stories.title: No India-US trade deal until new US tariff framework, Section 301 probe outcomes
stories.summary: Commerce Secretary says legal agreement is in final stages but clarity on comparative tariff advantages essential before signing pact
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The proposed India-US trade deal cannot be signed till Washington puts a new tariff architecture in place following the US Supreme Court’s dismantling of reciprocal and emergency tariffs, as comparative advantages offered to different countries need to be clear, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Wednesday.

The outcome of ongoing Section 301 investigations, which could lead to additional tariffs, also needs to be known as every country would want a trade deal that provides certainty on these probes, he said.

“The challenge that you need to appreciate is that the deal (framework for the first tranche of the bilateral trade agreement) was announced (in February) in the background of executive tariffs that were existing at that point of time.
Those tariffs have been struck down by the Supreme Court there.
Now a new tariff architecture is being created by the US,” Agrawal said at a FICCI event.

While the legal agreement has been negotiated and is in the final stages, and both sides want to conclude negotiations as quickly as possible, it cannot be signed until the new tariff architecture is in place, as this would determine the comparative advantages available to different countries.
“Until the tariff architecture comes back in place, signing of a deal, I think will take some time,” he said.
Agrawal also pointed to the implications of ongoing investigations under Section 301 of the US Trade Act of 1974, whose findings are expected in a few weeks or months.
“Every country will like to have a deal which gives them certainty around all the investigations that are going on.
You cannot have a deal till there are uncertainties around multiple investigations that are going on,” he said.

The Section 301 probes, including one into excess capacity under which India and several competing countries are being investigated, could result in penal duties and shape the new US tariff architecture, officials had earlier explained.

The India-US interim trade framework was announced on February 7, 2026, with Washington agreeing to lower its reciprocal tariff on Indian goods to 18 per cent from 25 per cent and roll back another 25 per cent penalty tariff imposed over New Delhi’s purchase of Russian oil.

stories.headline: Reel-makers can't claim immunity as journalists, Delhi Police tells Supreme Court
stories.title: Reel-makers can't claim immunity as journalists, Delhi Police tells Supreme Court
stories.summary: Reel-makers can't claim immunity as journalists, Delhi Police tells Supreme Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Delhi Police has told the Supreme Court that social media influencers and Reel-makers cannot claim the same protection as journalists covering protests, arguing that the intent behind their work must determine whether they qualify as reporters.
Social media influencers and Reel-makers cannot claim the same protection as professional journalists while filming protests, the Delhi.
Police has told the Supreme Court, arguing that carrying a camera and microphone does not automatically make someone a journalist.

In an affidavit filed before the Supreme Court, the police said the purpose behind a person's activity should be a key factor in determining whether they are engaged in journalism or merely creating social media content for commercial gain.
It argued that while journalists gather and report news, some content creators record events primarily to make Reels and videos for online platforms.

The affidavit was filed in response to a batch of petitions alleging that journalists were harassed, obstructed and detained while covering protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
The protests were organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
During earlier hearings, the Supreme Court had cautioned the Delhi.
Police against preventing journalists from covering the demonstrations, following complaints that media personnel were being stopped from performing their duties.
In its latest response, the police maintained that it had never knowingly interfered with genuine journalistic work.

"The Delhi Police has, at no point, sought to obstruct, impede or interfere with the bona fide discharge of journalistic duties, whether during the protests in question or otherwise," the affidavit said.

However, the affidavit argued that the court's earlier direction protecting journalists while covering protests was not intended to give social media influencers, Reel-makers or unruly protesters' exemption from police restrictions at prohibited assemblies.

stories.title: Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Enhancement Of District Judges' Superannuation Age
stories.summary: The States cannot raise the argument of financial burden to oppose the increase of retirement age, the Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The States cannot raise the argument of financial burden to oppose the increase of retirement age, the Court said.
The Supreme Court today reserved judgment in the All India Judges Association case with reference to the issue of enhancement in the superannuation age of District Judges to 62 years.

Upon being informed about certain States/UTs' opposition to the enhancement, the Court asked Attorney General R Venkataramani to make one last attempt to persuade the concerned authorities so that the proceedings can be closed on a good note.
The States/UTs that remained to come on board were given 2 weeks to revisit the issue.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was dealing with the All India Judges Association case, in which the Court had earlier directed all States/UTs to consider enhancing the retirement age of district judges to 61/62 years after consulting their respective High Courts.
(i) additional burden on State exchequer(ii) "heartburn" among other employees of the State/UT, and (iii) effect on legitimate aspirations of young entrants in judicial service.

At the time, the Court had rejected the financial burden argument, opining that retaining judicial officers for a few additional years would, in fact, defer the payment of retirement benefits, pension and other retiral dues, thereby reducing the immediate financial burden.
The Court said that this would be particularly beneficial for revenue-deficit States/UTs, describing the arrangement as a potential “bonanza” for them.

On the "heartburn" among other employees, the Court observed that services of government employees and judicial officers could not be equated (as the latter entered service at a substantially advanced age).

Today, Senior Advocate Siddharth Bhatnagar (Amicus) informed the Court that 15 States/UTs were now in favour of enhancement, while 12 continued to oppose and 4 (Gujarat, Jharkhand, Delhi and Puducherry) sought more time to arrive at a decision.
The States/UTs opposing the enhancement included Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Haryana, Bihar, Manipur, Meghalaya, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.
The Chief Justice opined that some of the States/UTs opposing the enhancement were "minor", but some required the intervention of AG Venkataramani - particularly UP and Rajasthan.

stories.headline: Bihar Cabinet approves ₹66.58 crore for DPR preparation for Buxar-Bhagalpur six-lane greenfield expressway
stories.title: Bihar Cabinet approves ₹66.58 crore for DPR preparation for Buxar-Bhagalpur six-lane greenfield expressway
stories.summary: The Cabinet also gave its nod to exempt in certain cases from the requirement of submitting Utilisation Certificates (UCs) following the amendment in Rules 271 and 272 of the Bihar Treasury Code, 2011.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Bihar cabinet on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) gave its nod to determine resource estimates, reserve prices and timelines to carry out e-auction of the Majos and Bhanta Magnetite (Iron Ore) block (re-auction) in Jamui district and the Pindara (Copper-Lead-Zinc) block in Banka district of the State.

The move is likely to fetch ₹5,053 crore to the State once the auction for the blocks is successfully completed, Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) Arvind Kumar Chaudhary told reporters in Patna in a post-Cabinet briefing.
Mr. Chaudhary said that the estimated value of blocks in Banka and Jamui have been pegged at ₹726 crore and ₹4,327 crore respectively.

Similarly, in another decision, it approved the allotment of two stone blocks, bearing block number 06 and 07, in favour of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), subject to the prescribed terms and conditions, Mr. Chaudhary said.
It will boost investment in the State, create new employment opportunities and give fresh momentum to Bihar’s industrial and economic prosperity.
RS 66.58 CR approved for six lane Buxar -Bhagalpur Greenfield Expressway.

In another decision, the state cabinet approved ₹66.58 crore for preparing the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Buxar-Bhagalpur six-lane greenfield expressway and engaging expert consultants, Mr. Chaudhary said.
The six-lane Buxar-Bhagalpur greenfield expressway will give fresh momentum to connectivity and development in Bihar.

The proposed expressway covered under the project will pass through the districts of Buxar, Bhojpur, Arwal, Jehanabad, Gaya, Nalanda, Sheikhpura, Munger, Lakhisarai, Nawada, Jamui, Banka and Bhagalpur in Bihar, he said.

The expressway will provide connectivity to the Purvanchal Expressway in the west and the Raxaul-Haldia Expressway in the east, he said adding that the expressway will form an integral part of and serve as a complementary link to the Delhi-Lucknow-Buxar-Bhagalpur-Haldia Corridor.
Its construction will ease travel, boost trade and investment, and create new opportunities for employment and regional development.
The implementation of the project will be carried out by the Bihar State Road Development Corporation Limited (BSRDCL), Patna.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea To Finalise Judges' Appointment MoP, Bring Collegium Minutes Under RTI
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea To Finalise Judges' Appointment MoP, Bring Collegium Minutes Under RTI
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 18) issued notice on a petition filed by NGO Lok Prahari seeking directions to the Union Government and the Chief Justice of India (CJI) to finalise the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) governing the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts, which has remained pending for nearly 11 years.
A bench of Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale issued notice to the respondents, including the Union Government and the Secretary General of the Supreme Court.
The bench also permitted the petitioner to file an amended petition.
Senior Advocate Sanjay Hegde appeared for Lok Prahari.
The Memorandum of Procedure lays down the process for the appointment, elevation and transfer of judges to the higher judiciary under the Collegium system.
It was first framed in 1999 following the Supreme Court's judgment in the Second Judges case.
The petition highlights the delay of nearly 11 years in finalising the revised MoP governing the appointment of judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts.

The petition states that subsequent to the 2015 judgment striking down the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), a five-judge Constitution Bench had directed that the existing MoP could be supplemented and finalised by the Government of India in consultation with the Chief Justice of India.

It identified important areas requiring improvement, including eligibility criteria for judicial appointments, transparency in the selection process, establishment of a permanent secretariat and a mechanism for dealing with complaints against prospective judges.

The petition has also sought directions to make the minutes of meetings of the Supreme Court and High Court Collegiums concerning judicial appointments accessible under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (RTI Act).

Lok Prahari has sought a direction to the CJI, on the administrative side, to make necessary changes to the existing MoP in accordance with the unanimous view of the Collegium, taking into consideration the factors identified by the Supreme Court's Constitution Bench in its December 16, 2015 order in the NJAC case.
It has further sought a direction to the Union Government to finalise the revised MoP within one month, in consultation with the CJI, after the latter takes a decision on the proposed changes.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Ban On Animal Sacrifices For Religious Rituals
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Ban On Animal Sacrifices For Religious Rituals
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today dismissed a public interest litigation seeking a ban on killing of animals in the name of religion.
A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan, and Justice Aparesh Singh passed the order on a petition filed by Advocate Shruti Bist.

The PIL was filed seeking a direction to the Ministry of Animal Husbandry to amend Section 28 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 so as to ban the killing of animals in the name of religion.

The PIL cited different forms of animal cruelty, including: neglect and abandonment, physical and emotional abuse, animal hoarding, ritualistic animal abuse, use of animals in entertainment, animal testing in laboratories, domestic violence and animal cruelty, and farm animal abuse.
The petition argued that animal sacrifice has been a longstanding tradition within Hindu rituals, especially in worshipping deities like Ma Durga and Ma Kali.
The practice waned with the rising influence of non-violence sentiment of Jainism and Buddhism, but later found its way back to Hinduism.

stories.headline: Supreme Court examines Lokpal's power to issue show-cause notices without hearing
stories.title: Supreme Court examines Lokpal's power to issue show-cause notices without hearing
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought a response from the Lokpal of India on a plea challenging a Delhi High Court verdict which held that the anti-corruption ombudsman was not required to provide a public servant an opportunity of hearing before issuing a show-cause notice with regard to an investigation.

The Delhi High Court, on April 15, had dismissed a petition filed by public servant Chinmoyjit Sen, who had challenged a Lokpal order dated February 25 and a subsequent show-cause notice issued on February 27 in connection with a complaint.

Observing that the right to be heard arises before any final action is taken under Section 20(3) of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the high court had held that the Lokpal was not required to provide a public servant an opportunity of hearing before issuing a show-cause notice.

Section 20(3) of the Act requires a Lokpal bench of at least three members to review preliminary inquiry reports under Section 20(2), hear the public servant, decide if a prima facie case exists and choose one or more actions.
The Lokpal probes allegations of corruption under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 against specified public servants, politicians and certain institutions.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submissions of Sen's lawyer and issued the notice to the ombudsman.
The bench, however, refused to stay the proceedings before the Lokpal against Sen and said that the matter would be taken up after a week.
The proceedings originated from a preliminary inquiry conducted by the CBI on the directions of the Lokpal.
The CBI submitted its preliminary inquiry report on January 27, following which the Lokpal examined the allegations and found certain of them against Sen to be prima facie substantiated.
The Lokpal subsequently issued a show-cause notice to the petitioner, calling upon him to respond to the two allegations and providing an opportunity of hearing under Section 20(3) of the Act.
Challenging the order and notice, Sen told the high court that the Lokpal had passed the February 25 order without giving him an opportunity of hearing.
It was further said that the Lokpal had already formed an opinion on the allegations, rendering the subsequent show-cause notice and hearing an empty formality.

stories.headline: CJI Surya Kant Meets UN Special Rapporteur On Rights Of Persons With Disabilities, Says Supreme Court Will Set Up Committee On Disability Rights
stories.title: CJI Surya Kant Meets UN Special Rapporteur On Rights Of Persons With Disabilities, Says Supreme Court Will Set Up Committee On Disability Rights
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court will set up a Permanent Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant announced on Wednesday.

The CJI also directed the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee to constitute panels of young lawyers and sign language interpreters to assist advocates with disabilities in proceedings before the Court.

The announcements were made during a meeting between the CJI and Ms. Heba Hagrass, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, at the Supreme Court on November 18.
Lawyers with disabilities and representatives of civil society also participated in the meeting.
Emphasising that ensuring the rights of persons with disabilities is a constitutional obligation, the CJI said that equality is a fundamental principle of the Constitution.
He stressed the need to identify gaps in the implementation of laws and policies to ensure that persons with disabilities can exercise their rights in practice.
Referring to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, Chief Justice Surya Kant acknowledged the steps taken by the Government and the judiciary over the past decade.
He also highlighted the role of courts in addressing administrative delays that prevent persons with disabilities from accessing benefits under laws and welfare schemes.
The CJI said that courts can issue writs of continuing mandamus directing public authorities to discharge their statutory obligations and monitor compliance until the required action is taken.
He further highlighted the contribution of public interest litigation in helping persons with disabilities enforce their rights.
Referring to Article 142 of the Constitution, he noted that the provision empowers the Supreme Court to do complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it.

The CJI also spoke about measures undertaken within the judiciary to promote the representation of persons with disabilities, including reservation in judicial and higher judicial services and relaxation of qualifying marks for eligible candidates with disabilities.

The CJI also directed the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee to constitute panels of young lawyers and sign language interpreters to assist advocates with disabilities in proceedings before the Court.

Lawyers with disabilities and representatives of civil society also participated in the meeting.
Emphasising that ensuring the rights of persons with disabilities is a constitutional obligation, the CJI said that equality is a fundamental principle of the Constitution.
He stressed the need to identify gaps in the implementation of laws and policies to ensure that persons with disabilities can exercise their rights in practice.
Referring to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, Chief Justice Surya Kant acknowledged the steps taken by the Government and the judiciary over the past decade.
He also highlighted the role of courts in addressing administrative delays that prevent persons with disabilities from accessing benefits under laws and welfare schemes.
The CJI said that courts can issue writs of continuing mandamus directing public authorities to discharge their statutory obligations and monitor compliance until the required action is taken.
He further highlighted the contribution of public interest litigation in helping persons with disabilities enforce their rights.

stories.headline: Amit Shah to inaugurate two-day ‘anti-terror conference’ in New Delhi tomorrow
stories.title: Amit Shah to inaugurate two-day ‘anti-terror conference’ in New Delhi tomorrow
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 18: In line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah will inaugurate the two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on Thursday, 19th November 2026. The conference is being organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, as a part of a continued effort to bolster the nation's collective response to terrorism. This year's conference will deliberate on the theme 'Cross-Border Terrorism'. Held annually, the conference has steadily grown into a significant gathering of operational forces, agencies working in the field of counter-terrorism, and experts from the technical, legal and forensic domains. It offers the agencies / forces, an opportunity to collectively examine matters that have bearing on national security and the threats arising from terrorism. In keeping with the 'Whole of Government approach', the conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders. It seeks to establish formal as well as informal channels that enable coordinated and concerted action against terrorism. The conference also aims at contributing substantive inputs towards the formulation of future policy. The conference sessions will address a range of subjects, including, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations, and the effective management of trials. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, and emerging hybrid threats to national security. Further sessions will examine the tools, techniques and case experiences involved in disrupting terror financing networks, as well as the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges. This year, the conference will also host a capacity-building training programme for State police personnel and practising professionals. The programme has been designed to equip participants in several areas. These include applying the new criminal laws in terror investigations, using digital evidence in prosecution, and trial strategy and management. The programme will also cover special provisions relating to the investigation of terror cases, common challenges posed by the defence, the protection of witnesses, and the initiatives taken by the Government to improve prosecution. Over the two days, the deliberations will enable law enforcement agencies to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations. The conference will be attended by senior police officers of States and Union Territories, officers of Central agencies and departments dealing with counter-terrorism, and experts from allied fields including law, forensics and technology.
